games.engine: N64 (native PC build from the Pilotwings64Decomp decompilation)
games.notes: Native PC port (Windows, Linux, experimental Android) that adds two-player split-screen to a single-player game; both players fly the same test with their own controller, HUD and score. Local only, MIT, bring your own ROM.

games.title: Crab Champions
games.notes: The game already has online co-op; CrabSync makes it one team run with a shared inventory, crystals, loadout and health pool (everyone dies together), and opens the solo-only Arcade and Holdout minigames to the lobby. Host-only install, every part can be switched off. Ships with CrabMods (new items) and a mod manager. MIT. Tied to one game build.

games.title: Half Sword
games.notes: Online multiplayer for a single-player game in one drop-in DLL. Steam lobbies and invites, each player simulates their own fighter, hits go through the game's own damage code, gore, grabs and dropped weapons synced; match modes, chat, spectating. Pre-release v0.4, first two-player test done and its fixes released. Tied to one game build.

games.title: Command & Conquer 3 Tiberium Wars
games.notes: Campaign missions run inside a multiplayer game (C&C Online or LAN) with both humans controlling the campaign side. Played by two people on GDI mission 1; mission flow, briefings and own factions per player not done. Unpublished; write-up in games/command-and-conquer-3.

games.title: Divinity II: Developer's Cut
games.notes: Build from zero toward split-screen co-op, two players on one PC, started 2026-10-18. Stage 1 done; the game loads a 32-bit dinput8.dll proxy (it imports only DirectInput8Create). Stage 2 done; per-instance Profile and Savegames redirection via a MinHook hook on SHGetFolderPathA, enabled by an env-var token; verified with two real game instances, the real profile untouched in every run. No co-op gameplay yet; running two instances at the menu is flaky (a startup race in the engine's main-menu movie player, a pre-existing bug, proven not the hook). The automated test covers the isolation layer only. Tied to one exe build (addresses in the write-up); the hook is build-independent by design. MIT. Code, notes and tests in this repo's game folder.

games.title: Stacklands
games.notes: Host-authoritative mirror on the official mod loader. Joiners' sims are frozen and their input is replayed on the host. LAN/IP is covered by a 13-check two-instance automated test; Steam lobbies are untested. Write-up in games/stacklands.

games.title: Enter the Gungeon
games.notes: Gungeon Online 0.101.0, MIT, drops into BepInEx. Steam lobby invites plus LAN UDP 27460. The host shares the run seed and the world/level/save state; enemy death and HP are synced but enemy attack simulation is not, so combat can drift. Verified with two real game clients over LAN using the mod's built-in test harness: both connected, picked different characters and generated the same floor (fingerprint 2A7BE448); a ~4 minute run had no disconnect or version mismatch. Write-up in games/enter-the-gungeon.

games.title: Enter the Gungeon
games.notes: GungeonTogether 3-Player 0.10.8, MIT, drops into BepInEx and needs the ModTheGungeon API 1.9.2. Steam lobbies plus Steam P2P, aimed at 3 or more players. Marked AI Generated on Thunderstore and early: the published DLL (assembly 0.10.8.0) is ahead of its public repo (still 0.9.0), so it was reviewed from the decompiled binary (no URLs, file writes, process launches or native imports found). Boot-tested here in an isolated copy: the plugin loads, Steam initialises and the P2P/lobby callbacks register, but a real 3-client play session was not run (needs three Steam accounts). Incompatible with Gungeon Online; remove GungeonOnline.dll. Write-up in games/enter-the-gungeon.

games.title: Clive Barker's Jericho
games.notes: Whole campaign, each player controls one squad member, AI keeps the rest; two players can share one PC in split screen. Version 0.3.0 (called Jericho Co-op before 0.2.4); the host is Ross's soul and the second player Jones's astral projection, both switching bodies as in the original, players 3-4 keep their character; display mode and refresh rate in the game's Video settings; starts without a mouse. Installer window and a shortcut that installs newer releases from GitHub before each start, in six languages. LAN/direct IP over ENet or Steam lobbies (runs as Spacewar), in a dinput8.dll proxy (two engine faults handled in memory, a split screen crash and a NULL read at the last boss; the exe file only gets the large-address-aware flag); host-authoritative enemies, story, scenes, powers, doors, breakable and movable objects and saves; each fire team follows its own player. The whole campaign runs in automated tests over a LAN between two PCs, every story split with a real host and client; a first human session over Steam (missions 1-8) was fixed up in 0.2.2, a full human playthrough is still to come. 0.3.0 goes through every weapon, fire mode, reload, melee strike and power of the seven playable characters and checks on screen what the watching player sees (the Bull's wind-up, second-weapon triggers, magazines), adds gestures for actions without a third-person animation, SMOD Add-ons compatibility and a single-file setup exe. MIT. The MAK-PIVO fork's (no longer public) Steam, shared QTE, sync and boss/power work was merged back in 0.2.1. Write-up in games/clive-barkers-jericho.

games.title: Poppy Playtime
games.notes: Build-from-zero UE4SS Lua mod plus a Python relay. Two real game clients over the UDP relay see each other as a player-shaped puppet (same mesh, material, scale, and a single-node walk animation) at the peer's reported position, both directions, checked by a scripted run with no crashes. Only movement is synced; the chapter cannot be finished together. The Steam transport initialises, logs on and creates/enters a lobby, but its P2P message leg is untested (needs a second Steam account). Prior art: a fan multiplayer mod was made and deleted by its author (dev confirmed on Reddit); Chapter 2 builds contain an unused multiplayer minigame documented by TCRF, and the Steam build ships the VoxeX voice SDK, so multiplayer code existed in-house. Work notes in games/poppy-playtime/.

games.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3
games.notes: Closed-source MW3 client focused on singleplayer/co-op plus multiplayer with bots and dedicated servers; both players need a Steam-owned copy. Its shared play is Spec Ops/Survival, not the campaign. A community Survival layer on top of it notes its Spec Ops co-op desyncs.

games.title: Far Cry 2
games.notes: No public Far Cry 2 co-op campaign project exists (searched 2026-10-19). Research prototype for Steam 1.03: a dinput8.dll proxy runs a Lua 4.0 channel and native commands inside the game, finds the player's Havok body by class, and exchanges position and heading over its own UDP socket; each copy spawns an invincible avatar of the peer, moves and turns it. A relay (in the probe's open PRs) carries this over Steam (Spacewar lobby, no IPs or port forwarding): one manual run between two PCs on different networks on 2026-10-25 kept a 16/s link for ~7 minutes with 0 dropped and the avatar followed the host's walk. Players see each other only as a sliding, idle-pose avatar: no animation, weapons, health, mission or world sync. Stock multiplayer cannot carry the campaign (Ubisoft services closed 2021-06-01; -join waits on gconnect.ubi.com). QA covers only the position puppet: a script (tests/two_copy_walk.ps1, in MortyRei/fc2-coop-probe#1-#3, not merged) drives two copies on one PC and checks positions and heading (20/20, 22/22 through relays; it fails on the probe before its fixes). Probe code is MIT, in its own repo; write-up and dated notes in games/far-cry-2.

games.title: Tainted Grail: The Fall of Avalon
games.notes: BepInEx 5 + Harmony, needs the game's Steam beta branch "mono". Both players load their own save; the host overlays story flags and places NPCs, drops are first grab wins. Latest build 0.5.36 (2026-07-28), no license file. Players report softlocks, combat desync and a gate that stays closed for the guest after the Odran dialogue; the author says only Act 1 was really tested. Last author reply on Nexus 2026-07-28, none to the comments from August on. Write-up in games/tainted-grail-the-fall-of-avalon.

games.title: Gothic 3
games.notes: Pigeonade project, version 0.3 reported by Gothic Up on 2026-09-19. Report describes Steam invitations and trading, requiring Steam plus CP 1.75.14. Release link leads to Discord. Current archive, license, source and exact supported executable hashes are not verified; this is a community report, not local QA.

games.title: Gothic 3
games.notes: Yevh v0.35.0-beta.1, tested on Steam CP 1.75.14 with shipped settings. Automated suite with two real clients on one PC: both join one campaign and shared quest state syncs both ways (3 of 3 PASS, negative control FAILs); see games/gothic-3. Shipped tuning turns off remote player bodies and NPC scene/death sync. Rejoining with a new game is refused by the mod. C++ core source not found in the archive or public tree.

games.title: Gothic 3
games.notes: Full Gothic 3 campaign co-op for two players, built from zero on the Gothic 3 SDK and ENet, GPL-3.0-or-later. Public beta v0.6.0 (2026-10-26) with setup in English, German and Polish. Shared: quests, dialogs and story, enemies and combat, loot and chests, trade between players, freed towns and story moves, town reputation, the clock and the host's saves; a downed player can be revived. Every feature is covered by bot suites driving two real game clients (187 runs for 0.6.0), and the bots played the story to Innos' ending. Needs Steam CP 1.75.14 and Parallel Universe Patch 1.1.1. Not yet played by people: the Adanos and Beliar endings and more than two players. See games/gothic-3.

games.title: Crimson Desert
games.notes: ASI mod (Ultimate ASI Loader) for Steam build 1.0.0.2976 / game version 2.03.02 only; turns itself off on other builds. Each player stays in their own save and sees the other; hostile enemies near the host are shared (experimental); quests, NPCs and items are not shared; Steam friends only. GPL-3.0. The author stopped work at v0.2.0 and invites others to continue it. A revival focused on shared quest progress is claimed in cranebeaker/coop-anything#51: builds on Linux with clang-cl + xwin, one-PC echo smoke test ran under Proton (no automated two-player test yet). Research and dated notes in games/crimson-desert.

games.title: Crimson Desert
games.notes: Version 0.2.3 "in development" per its README: player 2 takes over a companion slot on the host; position, enemy HP and some mount state sync are claimed; quest, cutscene and world-interaction sync are not applied. Source is public but the repository has no license. Last push 2026-07-08. Claims are the author's; not tested here.

games.title: Crimson Desert
games.notes: Unreleased; known only from press coverage of test footage (players see each other's moves and can damage the same enemy; NPC and enemy placement differs between the two worlds). No public build or code found 2026-10-19.

games.title: Fear & Hunger
games.notes: Each player runs the game from their own copy in a browser window; a small Node server overlays the mod as plugins. Players control separate characters who can split up or fight together; world switches are shared by a census built from the game's data. Online play through a Cloudflare quick tunnel and a keyed link, no port forwarding. Optional AI partner. Every release passes a gate of about 50 suites driving two or more real game clients. MIT, made with Claude.

games.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2
games.notes: COD-MOD 3.223 DLL (open source, no license, momo5502, re-enables the Spec Ops co-op netcode over direct IP) plus a closed x_coop.ff with campaign script changes by an unknown author, shared as a mega.nz pack used with Hamachi. Needs the 32-bit 1.0.159 build, so it no longer runs on the 64-bit Steam build of 2026. Players report freezes and rough missions; details in games/modern-warfare-2.

games.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2
games.notes: Beta (v0.5.0-beta), playable. MIT mod for the 64-bit Steam build. A winmm.dll proxy plus load-time GSC patches on top of the game's own lockstep Spec Ops co-op netcode, hosted and joined from the game's menus (lobby, LAN list, address, Steam invite). Every set piece is reworked for two players, among them S.S.D.D., Team Player, Wolverines!, the rope and rappel scenes (Gulag, Just Like Old Times, Escape from Favela), Takedown's car, The Only Easy Day's swim, Cliffhanger's climb and snowmobiles, No Russian, Second Sun's crash and ISS, Loose Ends' betrayal, Endgame's boat and knife fight; enemies fight both players, both play the difficulty the host picks, friendly fire is a lobby switch and every level has checkpoints. The game's co-op runs in lockstep (both PCs run the same level), so the world is shared. In-game QA on two copies, including a bot tour of the start points of all 19 levels (the Museum epilogue still fails for player 2); two people played parts of the story on two PCs, from the start up to and including No Russian. The missions after it were checked by bots only; not played through end to end yet. Write-up in games/modern-warfare-2.

games.title: Celeste
games.notes: Helper library for CelesteNet. Adds entities and triggers (spawn points, switches, gates and more) whose state synchronizes between players, which is what makes shared-objective co-op maps possible. Also ships a beta "Co-op Everywhere" mode that swaps supported vanilla entities for synchronized versions. Source on GitHub (corkr900); the GameBanana release v1.1.4 is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Partnership depends on it.

games.title: Celeste
games.notes: Two-player co-op mini campaign built on CelesteNet plus Co-op Helper, and the closest thing to a playable co-op campaign today. The mod page says it is designed for exactly two players, says it should not be possible in single-player, and recommends a private channel so only you and your partner share the map. Depends on MaxHelpingHand and LunaticHelper. Release v1.0.1 (2022-01); the GameBanana release is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 and no source repo was found.

games.title: Celeste
games.notes: Two-player co-op Summit map, death-link style and aimed at Expert to Grandmaster players, by Clantis. Pulls a large dependency tree (fourteen helper mods including Co-op Helper and MaxHelpingHand), so it is much heavier to install than Partnership; treat it as optional. Release v1.1.3 (2026-10); the GameBanana release is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Its dependencies were not installed or tested here.

games.title: Dave the Diver
games.notes: Same-screen co-op in one game instance (BepInEx 6 IL2CPP). Player 2 is a clone of Dave on the right side of the keyboard or an Xbox controller; no networking. Dives and the sushi bar only. An in-game test bot with a mutation pass covers creature grabs on both divers; the sushi bar and the newest grab fixes are hand-tested. MIT. Write-up in games/dave-the-diver.

games.title: Dave the Diver
games.notes: Online co-op over direct UDP, host-authoritative (BepInEx IL2CPP). Its README lists synced fish, pickups, world objects, mission and story progress and the sushi bar, and says it is in active development with occasional desyncs; it also lists bosses, DLC and reconnects as not supported yet. No GitHub releases. MIT.

games.title: Dave the Diver
games.notes: Fork of S1ii's Coop-Divers (BepInEx 6 be.790, IL2CPP) with Steam online play (friends-only lobby plus SteamNetworkingMessages through Valve's relay, called from steam_api64.dll directly) and LAN as the fallback, plus fixes for Steam build 26209260. A two-copy lab suite (19 checks over LAN, the Steam path through a SteamMock, and 120 ms lag with 5% loss) passes, and every check has a mutant that must fail it. Diver HP, oxygen and weapons are not synced and clients can't damage bosses. Releases are pre-releases (v0.19.3) until two Steam accounts have played a full session. MIT. Write-up in games/dave-the-diver.

games.title: Pacific Drive
games.notes: Two-player alpha on Unreal's own listen-server netcode, driven by a UE4SS Lua mod, with an installer that sets up UE4SS, updates the mod from GitHub releases and collects logs (release v0.8.0). Automated two-instance tests pass for joining and rejoining, riding as a passenger, map travel, shared world items, a shared car trunk, car part health, fuel and battery following the host, item state (fuel, charge, durability), player 2's refuel and charge, player 2's saved inventory, and down/revive/team death; one live session over the internet (Radmin VPN) was played. In progress on the main branch, the host's generated zone content (abandoned cars, props, doors, containers) replicated to player 2, door state shared both ways, lootable containers holding the host's items. Not synced yet are quests and progress, hazards and weather, and which car parts are installed; player 2 cannot drive. Host needs UDP 7777 reachable. Steam build 21896301. MIT.

games.title: BattleTech
games.notes: In development by a dev on the Co-op Anything Discord, who posts progress in the project's topic there. No public build yet.

games.title: Half-Life: Alyx
games.notes: In development by a dev on the Co-op Anything Discord. The dev reports networking and object sync working, with enemy sync being polished; other players show as an NPC model for now, and testing uses a non-VR mod. No public build yet.

games.title: Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade
games.project: Final Fantasy VII Remake and Rebirth Co-op (Co-op Anything Discord)
games.notes: In development by a dev on the Co-op Anything Discord, who has shown it running in Final Fantasy VII Rebirth and plans to release a version for Remake. No public build yet.

games.title: Spider-Man: Friend or Foe
games.project: Spider-Man: Friend or Foe Co-op (Co-op Anything Discord)
games.notes: Online co-op in development by a dev on the Co-op Anything Discord: each player on their own PC and screen, with keyboard or controller, without Parsec or Steam Remote Play. No public build yet. Relationship to the separately listed native research project and its exact engine identity are unverified.

games.title: Deep Rock Galactic: Survivor
games.notes: Local co-op for two controllers on one PC (a BepInEx 6 IL2CPP plugin; the second dwarf is a second player object in the same game process). Licence: MIT. It has no network code of its own; online play with a friend only works through Steam Remote Play Together (Steam's own streaming; the invite works, not tested screen by screen). Elimination and Escort missions. Automated QA, one PC, test copy of the game with virtual gamepads (harness in the repo, tools/batch_*.ps1), every check has a twin flag that turns it red. Results 2026-10-21 to 2026-10-23 (run ids in the repo's PLAN.md): main menu 11/11, real mouse clicks 5/5, real start from the menu (class and mission read back from the live second dwarf), menu locks 10/10 (twin 6 ok, 4 fail), bonus mirror 5/5 (twin 0/5), pause menu per player 5/5 (twins red), retry run 7/7, revive and loot-crate tests green (twins red). The author has also played several full runs by hand with two controllers: no game-breaking bugs, at most small visual ones such as a wrong UI display; no independent report yet. Known gaps in the repo README (end-screen damage numbers probably inaccurate, DLCs not supported and not tested). Release 1.0.0 with installer.

games.title: Little Nightmares
games.notes: In development by a dev on the Co-op Anything Discord. The dev reports that enemies now react to the second player; keeping doors and passages open for the second player is the next step. No public build yet.

games.title: Yu-Gi-Oh! 5D's Tag Force 4
games.project: Yu-Gi-Oh! 5D's Tag Force 4 Co-op (Co-op Anything Discord)
games.notes: In development by a dev on the Co-op Anything Discord, who posts progress in the project's topic there. The game is a 2009 PSP release. No public build yet.

games.title: Graveyard Keeper
games.notes: BepInEx 5 + Harmony, host-authoritative, over Steam lobbies and P2P with its own reliable layer, plus LAN discovery. The host's save is sent to the client. README lists shared time, weather, quests, crafting, world objects, combat, drops, zones, workers, dungeons, fishing, dialogue and cutscenes, and DLC support; each player keeps their own inventory. Latest release 1.2.0 Beta (2026-09-04). A 9-test two-client suite (join, shared intro cutscene, movement, sleep, eating from a quick slot, ping) passes on 432b1d0 plus three fixes sent upstream as pull requests; without them a client can't use food from its own inventory (issue 22). MIT. Write-up in games/graveyard-keeper.

games.title: Graveyard Keeper
games.notes: BepInEx 5 + Harmony over a friends-only Steam lobby and P2P, with its own reliability layer. README lists movement, time, chopping, foraging, garden beds, graves, corpse carrying, building, crafting, shared chests and weather; the second player has a personal save and their own quest journal over the host's world, and NPC villagers and dungeon mobs are not synced yet. Latest build v0.1.5-test2 (2026-08-30, pre-release). Players report a client desync with NullReferenceException spam, a host soft lock and large-item duplication. The repo ships Steamworks.NET.dll and a 14 KB Stitch.dll in Multiplayer/lib. The author also wrote the reliable transport in Back From The Grave. MIT.

games.title: MDK2 HD
games.notes: Native dinput8.dll bridge plus Lua injected through settings.lua. The host runs the world; clients mirror enemies, replay shots including delayed Doganboy grenades, share pickups, doors and checkpoints, follow level loads, and revive at a partner when they go down. Cutscenes start together with a skip vote. Steam friends-only lobbies (invite or lobby ID, no port forwarding) or direct UDP, chosen in a launcher. Co-op saves and reconnect after a crash. Text chat, pings, proximity voice, difficulty and controls presets, character and emote wheels, couch (split-screen) co-op. Public alpha v0.2.0-alpha with an installer; before it, an automated ladder of 31 gates including all 96 checkpoints with two real clients and a host/client state diff.

games.title: Resident Evil 2 (2019 remake)
games.notes: Local split-screen only, built on Local Couch Co-op. REFramework Lua script plus a small pad DLL spawns up to three extra player characters, each with its own camera and screen quarter, inventory and settings. Shared weapon and ammo pickups, key and story items go to player 1, enemies target the nearest player, revive when downed, each player's room stays loaded within player 1's area. Test build v0.5.0.

games.title: The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion
games.notes: Local split-screen only, for the 2006 GOTY Steam build with xOBSE 22. A C++ xOBSE plugin draws the world twice, once per player camera, and gives player 2 (an NPC to the game) the player's rules where the engine only knew one player. One world, one time of day, player 2 on a leash around player 1, quests and journal are player 1's. Beta 0.9.1. Announced as MPL-2.0 with source on GitHub to follow; no repo found at check time.

games.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops III
games.engine: IW engine (Call of Duty, Treyarch fork)
games.notes: Raises the PC game's own 2-player local split screen to 4, as on console, for offline Zombies and Multiplayer with bots. An ezz BOIII client plugin relocates every per-local-client array that is [2] on PC to a [4] copy and widens the loops, using the PS4 build as the reference. Public domain (The Unlicense), with a list of client changes for native support.

games.title: Spider-Man: Friend or Foe
games.notes: Published two-player local co-op on one computer; contemporary PC reviews report no native online play. The separate research entries do not change this scope.

games.title: Spider-Man: Friend or Foe
games.project: Friend or Foe Online (native Windows research)
games.notes: Source-only Windows prototype targeting two independent clients. English/Russian bot checks used two processes on one PC and mock transport; Steam delivery and complete co-op remain unverified. No playable release.

games.title: Dave the Diver
games.notes: Windows installer (BepInEx 6 IL2CPP plus .NET runtime, checksum-verified) for the Coop-Divers online mod, plus a separate experimental Steam-invite prototype with friends-only lobbies and a host/join overlay, and a Linux/Steam Deck (Proton) install script. In the prototype the partner avatar only mirrors movement on the boat and in the sushi bar; world and story state are not shared. The README says a two-client connection has not been verified. MIT.

games.title: World of Goo
games.notes: Local two-player split screen on one PC for the Steam 1.5 build (20824155); player 1 mouse, player 2 gamepad. The PC exe still holds the Wii version's multi-cursor code (four mice, four cursors, per-player held balls); an SDL2.dll proxy feeds the second mouse from a pad and renders levels twice with a camera per half, one shared simulation. Settings in wogcoop.ini, reloaded live. Tested by the owner on chapter 1 (mouse + DualSense) plus scripted bot checks; other chapters, the time bug with two players and menus are unchecked. MIT.

games.title: Autonauts
games.notes: First beta (0.13.0). BepInEx 5 plugin, host-authoritative mirror (joiner sims frozen, input replayed on the host). Host and join from the game's own menus (Esc > Host Multiplayer; main menu > Multiplayer), Steam lobbies and invites plus direct IP (TCP 27015). Joiners build with undo, teach and program bots, use building menus, bot server, groups, catapult, spaceport, planning and the Creative spawn menu; characters are stored with the host's save while away. Automated suites with real game clients on one PC (2 players 116/116, 4 players 46/46, own late-game save 18/18); one two-PC Steam session over the internet by the author. MIT. Write-up in games/autonauts.

games.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers
games.engine: Stormfront Fusion (Xbox), static recompilation to PC (The Two Towers Recompiled, xboxrecomp)
games.project: Two Towers couch co-op (on The Two Towers Recompiled)
games.notes: Local couch co-op (two controllers on one PC, one shared camera, no networking), built on The Two Towers Recompiled by Gumpolas. Player 2 has their own hero, controller, weapons, ammo, experience and upgrades; both play the story levels, with post-level stats and shops for both. Source only (MIT, a fork of the port), built from the player's own US retail game; tested with a 14-scenario bot suite (73 checks, all passing) on the port's 1.9.4.

games.title: Little Inferno
games.notes: Local two-player co-op on one PC for the Steam build 10124709 (2.0.3); player 1 mouse, player 2 gamepad (DualSense, DualShock 4, XInput), one fireplace, shared coins and save, like the Switch edition. The engine already keeps a second pointer (touch leftover); a winmm.dll proxy feeds it from the pad after each input poll and draws its cursor with D3D11. Menus outside the fireplace are player 1 only. Checked through the tutorial and first letters by scripted screenshots and an owner playtest; later catalogs, the ending and Ho Ho Holiday are unchecked. MIT.

games.title: The Witness
games.engine: In-house engine (Thekla); family not confirmed from the binary
games.notes: Dev preview, not playable with friends yet (no installer or release; localhost only). A proxy AnselSDK64.dll loaded by the game hooks Direct3D 11 Present and draws the other player as a puppet; two game copies exchange camera pose over UDP. Solving a panel in one game marks it solved in the other and opens the gated door by calling the game's own door function (events are numbered, acknowledged and resent). Tested on two tutorial door puzzles and one panel power-on chain, Steam build 11370412. Panel power-on progression and one cable lit by a tutorial maze use their own reliable events; a fresh or reloaded game resyncs from its peer. Power-off switching, other cables, plates, lasers and bridges remain unsynced. QA is an in-process bot (no focus, no desktop input) with a state diff over all panels and doors and baseline, loss, mutant, peer-restart, late-join, save-reload, second-door, power-on and cable scenarios. Coverage remains narrow, three tutorial puzzles (see games/the-witness). No other co-op work was found; the MIT-licensed witness-randomizer and witness-trainer, which read and write the running game, were the starting point.

games.title: Obscure
games.engine: Hydravision in-house (.hvp archives, .hoe scripts); not RenderWare
games.notes: Online co-op over Steam for the Steam version (build 215286), built on the game's own 2-player local co-op. A proxy xinput1_3.dll makes the friend's controller the host's player 2 and mirrors the host's game to the friend's copy (characters, enemies, items, doors, story flags, levels, weapons, inventory, deaths, save loading), with smoothing over the internet. Optional in-game supersampling, 16x filtering, a tuned ReShade setup and 16:9 widescreen. Ladders, racks and locks do not animate on the friend's screen. Bot tests drive two real copies on one PC (load, death, doors, items, combat) but only ran on builds up to 1.0; builds 1.1 to 1.8 (smoothing, graphics, widescreen) were not bot-tested, only checked by screenshots, measurements and playtests over Steam. MIT. Write-up in games/obscure.

games.title: The Last of Us Part II Remastered
games.notes: No public download as of 2026-10-23. Online co-op for No Return first, then the story campaign. A demo showed two players in the safe house with movement, animations, weapons, backpack, flashlights, melee, enemy AI and damage synced. Promised free and open source; no repository found yet.

games.title: The Last of Us Part II Remastered
games.notes: Two-PC story co-op where player 2 takes the chapter companion. v0.1.0 (2026-10-17) has a tested network layer, teleport, roster, overlay and loader, but the README says the game link is not mapped, so characters cannot be moved in game yet. Targets the 2025-04-03 launch build (PE timestamp 67ED75F7). Public source has no license file. The optional internet relay was not tested here.

games.title: The Last of Us Part II Remastered
games.notes: PvP and experimental co-op work shown from January to September 2026; reached 4v4, five maps, loadouts and leaderboards. Cancelled on 2026-09-14 after a letter from Sony Interactive Entertainment requesting it not be released. Never released; do not revive.

games.title: The Last of Us Part II Remastered
games.notes: One-commit experiment. Injects a DLL, syncs position between two instances over local UDP and spawns a visual clone of Ellie on F10, but there is no independently controlled second player and no NPC state sync. Not functional. Public source has no license file.

games.title: Night in the Woods
games.project: Night in the Woods Co-op prototype
games.notes: Experimental host/client prototype. One-off loopback checks are not a verified playable release; normal dialogue choices, scripted effects, persistent saves, and a full story run remain unverified.

games.title: StarCraft II: Wings of Liberty
games.notes: External launcher that runs the retail Wings of Liberty campaign maps of custom campaigns (WoL@Kit fan campaigns and mods that keep Blizzard's campaign scripts) as two-player games through Blizzard's s2client API, on each player's own install; both share player 1's army (or, on maps made for it, each has their own), each has their own hub. Steam relay (Spacewar app id) or direct IP with UPnP. Code (MIT) and test releases since 2026-10-23. One-PC smoke test (each mission launched from the hub, won by test command, back to the hub) passed for all 29 missions of one WoL@Kit campaign and of three campaigns on Blizzard's scripts, and 4 missions of a fourth; two-PC sessions by testers.

games.title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (TMNT)
games.notes: Local couch co-op on one PC for the PC game (TMNTGame.exe 1.0.0.188), two controllers, one shared midpoint camera, one game process. Work in progress, not stable. An injected DLL spawns an idle brother (or clones player 1's turtle and unshares its skeleton in solo-turtle levels like Level 1) and swaps the game's 584-byte pad and wrapper buffer around the input pipeline and player 2's AI tick when a second pad is connected; enemies target player 2, it has a health bar, and air leapfrog plus ground charged team attacks work with player 2 as partner. The partner's single-player exit leap after a team move is cut at the release frame, so it lands where it stands instead of flying off and snapping back. Rough edges remain (the cloned turtle in solo levels misses its katana scabbards, looks identical to Leonardo and uses a slightly different attack combo index, and scripted self-tests only cover the start of Level 1). Not released.

games.title: Tony Hawk's Underground 2
games.notes: Story Mode for two online on top of THEMOD 1.3 (a dinput8.dll proxy plus one QB script). The friend joins the host's story; cutscenes, goal cameras, won goals, guest swaps and the pro teammate are synced, and shared goals are won once both finish them. Skater stats stay per player. Ships a byte patcher that rebuilds THEMOD 1.3's exe from the player's own THUG2.exe, since THEMOD can no longer be downloaded. The tester and a friend play it online; a scripted two-client walkthrough checks for crashes only. MIT. Write-up in games/tony-hawks-underground-2.

games.title: Gedonia
games.notes: BepInEx 5 / HarmonyX plugin for the original Gedonia (Steam app 1114220, build 16727998; not Gedonia 2), built from zero. Steam P2P through the game's own Steamworks.NET (friends-only lobby of 4, in-game invites) or plain UDP in the home network (LAN discovery). Host-authoritative: enemies, followers and world events have one tester with epochs; story calls (dialogue answers, triggers) run on every machine in the host's order; shared conversations with voting; groups (combat XP and map markers per group); enemy scaling by group size near the enemy (host's settings); trading as a two-phase commit with the host as coordinator; spell effects and transformations shown to others; cutscenes start when every player confirms; chests, gathering spots, expeditions with seeded generated dungeons, travellers, time and weather, sounds; respawn crystals replace the reload-only death screen. QA: two game clients on one PC driven by test steps and bots (scripts/test-local.ps1, 38 scenarios, logged assertions and screenshots); real sessions of the tester with friends over Steam went fine, their findings fixed in 0.7. Each player keeps their own save. Write-up in games/gedonia/. MIT licence.

games.title: Code Vein
games.project: codevein-coop (CoopSeamless, CoopProbe, CoopNative; work in progress)
games.notes: Extends the game's own host + 1 guest Steam session instead of replacing it (UE4SS Lua plus a native MinHook DLL, MIT). Host re-signals and guests re-join automatically after field deaths, host deaths, boss-room deaths and boss kills; co-op works in areas whose boss is dead. In two-PC tests a guest who dies for good stays in the host's world, spectates and respawns next to the host at the host's next Mistle rest; the host can rest in co-op; the guest gets his own Mistle menu and can level up there; a host Mistle teleport takes the guest along. Not released. UE 4.18, Denuvo present, UE4SS works with HookLoadMap = 0.

games.title: Code Vein
games.notes: Per a forum reply, it only lets the host send distress signals in areas whose boss is dead; the guest is still removed on boss death and fog walls remain. The mod page itself was not checked.

games.title: Genesis Alpha One
games.notes: Build-from-zero UE4SS Lua prototype on the Epic Games Store build (UE 4.23). Uses the engine's own netcode: GameNetDriver is pointed at IpNetDriver (the shipped SteamNetDriver is missing in the Epic build), host reopens the map with ?listen. The mod copies the host's runtime ship level instances to the guest, hides the HUD fade left black by the join and initializes the guest's character. A string channel (ServerChangeName / ClientMessage) forwards the guest's input actions to the host: the guest walks, switches and fires weapons with real damage on both sides, sees its own shots, has its own health bar, hit feedback and hints. Death and crew promotion for the guest are in progress; lockers, terminals, PDA and map do not work for the guest yet. Tested manually with two instances on one PC. MIT. Write-up in games/genesis-alpha-one.

games.title: Baldi's Basics Plus
games.notes: Host-authoritative co-op for game version 0.14.5 Hide & Seek runs (BepInEx 5 and MelonLoader builds that play together). Syncs players (directional sprites, names, pings), every named NPC and its abilities, doors, windows, notebooks, free pickups, teammates' item effects, Johnny's shop with a shared YTP wallet, elevator results, individual capture with teammate spectating, and LAN host migration. LAN over TCP, or online through the game's own Steamworks.NET (Steam lobbies, invites, Valve relay; no host migration there). Random events follow the host (fog, Mystery Room, ruler and time-out mirrored; others host-only); field trips get the same Pitstop on every copy; challenges and Endless are not validated. MIT. v0.9.2 pre-release. The lab suite drives two and three real game processes (tours plus two-process LAN, NPC, soak and chaos-proxy link tests); the Steam transport ran on Steam's in-process socket pair under one account, and no two-account Steam session has run yet. The author's own hands-on testing (not yet with friends) found it mostly works well.

games.title: MiSide
games.notes: BepInEx 6 (be.790, Unity.IL2CPP) plugin for the Steam build. The host leads the story and clients follow; story events (presses, triggers, dialogue choices, keypads) are relayed rather than state, and the host runs every cutscene on its own clock. Players see each other as the main character with the full 68-bone pose. Interactions that put an item in the hand are done by the presser only; the rest play the same animation on every player's own character. Mita and NPCs are host-driven; chasers hunt each player locally, and a death restarts everyone at the checkpoint. Shared key inventory, seeded randomness, room objects, minigame end events, the Scene 18 visual novel; host migration; joins wait for the next chapter. The Scene 13/15 core computer and the Scene 14 PC game are run by one operator and replayed on every copy; the Scene 14 phone character and the Scene 1 phone app (dialogue, name, days, shop, cooking result, money) follow their holder or the host, and the phone shows in the holder's hand for the others. The handheld Tetris is each player's own. Steam P2P through the game's own steam_api64 (friend lobbies, Valve relay), LAN discovery or direct TCP 27030. v0.3.5 pre-release (v0.3.2 is the last full release). The lab suite drives 2-4 game copies on one PC (34 tours, including all of Scene 1 played to Scene 2, plus an every-chapter interaction run, 18 of 18 chapters). The author has played it with two friends (three players over Steam on separate PCs and accounts); their 19 reports fed the 0.3.5 fixes. Source is public with no licence file yet.

games.title: Spooky's Jump Scare Mansion: HD Renovation
games.notes: BepInEx 5 and MelonLoader 0.7 builds that play together, for the Steam build. The host picks every room (seeded room randomness) and runs every specimen; a transpiler retargets each specimen at the nearest standing player, including specimens that keep the player in a variable. One shared copy of the run's keys and inventory with a 10 s checksum repair; pickups, unlocks and weapons (the axe) shared, hits relayed to every copy, specimen and Taker damage decided on the host. Endings take the whole team; downed players spectate and revive at the next room. Covers the base mansion, Endless, the hospital and the Dollhouse. Taker boss attacks, health, stamina and some puzzle props are per player or refresh on re-entry; no host migration. Steam P2P through the game's own Steamworks (lobbies, invites, Valve relay) or LAN/direct TCP 27020. v0.2.11 pre-release. The lab suite runs up to four minimized game copies (mixed loaders) through scripted tours with error, heap, desync and frame-cost checks, plus a mutation check per fix; the author has also played it four-player with friends on separate Steam accounts and reports it works very well. Source is public with no licence file yet.

games.title: Crime Scene Cleaner
games.notes: BepInEx 6 be.791 IL2CPP plugin for Steam build 26046462. Co-op screen in the main menu (host or join a Steam friend, pick a save slot); the client follows the host into jobs, both leave together, laptop jobs reach both, each keeps their own report, money and skills. Shared items, bodies (carry, throw, van), blood cleaning and new stains, trash and bags, doors, drawers, lifts, power, conveyors, hacking terminals, furniture back in place and knocked over, evidence, valuables, secrets, cassettes, shards, story objects and objective flags; the other player is a skinned figure with the tool in hand and a carried body on the shoulder. Two players finished chapters 1-6 together (0.4.1); 0.4.2 fixes checked on one job and by bot suites (two game copies on one PC over localhost UDP driving items, stains, bodies, doors, trash, world machinery, jobs, laptop mails, the CCTV laptop and a mutant run). Known gaps - deleted CCTV recordings are per player; 3-4 players, Nightmare and the last chapters untested. MIT. Write-up in games/crime-scene-cleaner.

games.title: Dead Cells
games.notes: Local co-op on one PC with two controllers (no networking), a code mod for Dead Cells Core Modding (DCCM) 35.14.1 on game version 35 (Steam). A second real hero with its own health, flasks, gear, mutations, scrolls and HUD; shared camera on the players' midpoint; down and revive; per-player copies of loot, starting weapons and reward-room choices; menus, forge, pause screen and outfit room work on player 2's pad; shared keys; doors, boss arenas and teleporters bring the partner along, plus an L3 regroup. The owner played v0.6.0 from the start of a run to the Bank; v0.7 and v0.8 (fixes for that run, controller picker, per-player outfits) are not yet played. No automated tests. Player 2 has no visible head. MIT license. Write-up in games/dead-cells.

games.title: Dead Cells
games.notes: In active development (584 commits, last one 2026-10-19 when checked); no release was tested by us. Online host and client on DCCM (direct TCP port 1234 or Steam P2P). The remote player is shown as a ghost entity (GhostKing, a KingSkin), not a second real hero; no local play. MIT. Its Steam Workshop item showed as removed for violating Steam's guidelines when checked (reason not given), as did DCCM's own Workshop item.

games.title: Forager
games.notes: Online co-op for up to 4 players (host and 3 guests) as one native version.dll next to Forager.exe (proxy DLL with MinHook hooks into the YYC-compiled game; no game files changed). Steam build 6160665 only (in-game 4.1.9). Join by Steam invite (friends-only lobby, Steam P2P), LAN discovery or IP. Host-authoritative world; other players are puppet objPlayer instances, and the host runs a guest's actions through the game's own code by swapping the instance PlayerFind returns. Shared world, enemies, buildings, chests, islands, time and weather, level and XP, coins, skill tree, museum, NPC quests and dungeons; inventory, gear, familiars and costume per player. Classic worlds only; the Void trial does not work in co-op. Scripted tests drive 2 to 4 real game clients on one PC with PASS/FAIL checks and mutation twins; nine two-PC playtests, eight over Steam. 3 and 4 players tested only as copies on one PC. MIT. Write-up in games/forager.

games.title: Metroid Prime 2: Echoes
games.engine: Wii in Dolphin (Gecko and patch code injection)
games.notes: Local split-screen campaign for 2-4 players in the Metroid Prime Trilogy NTSC-U build (R3ME01 rev 0) on Dolphin, built on Echoes' versus mode with Gecko codes and a Dolphin patch. Any player opens doors and the others follow; shared items, scans and lives; save stations, Scan Visor, cutscenes, the map and enemy/boss targeting work for every player; difficulty codes (Hypermode by default). Playtested through the opening hours; later rooms surveyed by a test harness. Local split screen only; Dolphin NetPlay untested. Revives the abandoned 2019 asset-only attempt by SubsonicBeatz154. Write-up in games/metroid-prime-2-echoes.

games.title: ReStory: Chill Electronics Repairs
games.notes: BepInEx 5 plugin for game 1.0.033r (Steam). Co-op in the host's save (shared room, stock, wallet, mail, quests, courier boxes; each player's own bench; day ends when both agree) and a versus race mode. The other player is shown as a name and avatar, not as a character in the shop. Two-copy bot tests 78/78 co-op, 70/70 versus; played by two players on two PCs through Porthole. A Steam lobby route exists; no two-account session yet. MIT.

games.title: BattleTech
games.notes: Work in progress (pre-alpha, MIT), a ModTek mod for the Steam build 1.9.1. Combat is lockstep on the game's own versus-multiplayer invocation messages, routed through the host, with desync detection; Campaign and Career missions reach the guest as an in-memory combat save. Every player can command every 'Mech of the shared lance. Between missions the guest sees the host's company and its refits, pilot training, hiring, store, storage and company customization go to the host (and the host's back) without a reload. Not done: no per-player lances yet, travel and time are host-only; the shared mission opening (0.0.13) is tested on ordinary contracts only. Automated two-copy tests plus human sessions over Steam (two players).

games.title: Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain
games.notes: The one MGSV co-op mod people report actually playing; 2-player, early-development, Windows and Linux/SteamOS. Built on the game's own FOB online path, so a Steam P2P session connects host and client by SteamID (Steam network required). Host-authoritative; player 0 is the host and enemy AI and targeting are driven by the host. Bundles a local master server (fuse) on port 6667 so co-op records are not sent to Konami's server, and copies your save so single-player data stays safe. Uses an IHHook base for native patches but is not Infinite-Heaven-based and conflicts with mods touching the same files. Latest release v0.6.0 (2025-10-31), master ahead to 2026-09. Must roll the game back past the 2026-06-09 Steam patch, which breaks launch (issue 136). Mission-based from a curated list, no free roam yet, and more than 2 players fails to start. Partial sync; enemy positions/FOV, objectives, markers, vehicles, buddies and animations have known desyncs across 55 open issues. GPL-3.0 with the Commons Clause. Write-up and research in games/metal-gear-solid-v.

games.title: Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain
games.notes: Aims for up to 16 players (1 host + 15 clients) in the open world, Windows and Linux/Proton, using the game's own online functionality and the Steamworks SDK. As of 2026-10-25 the README states "Nothing is playable yet" - organization, docs, website and desk research are in place and the first 2-player build (0.1) is planned. GPL-3.0-only (docs CC BY-SA 4.0); clean-room IP policy. Created 2026-10-21. Write-up in games/metal-gear-solid-v.

games.title: Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain
games.notes: Placeholder repo created 2026-10-25 with a one-line README; co-op named as the first target, no code yet. CC0-1.0. Listed so the next agent can watch it. Write-up in games/metal-gear-solid-v.

games.title: Planetbase
games.notes: BepInEx 5 (x86) plugin for Planetbase 1.4.2, host-authoritative mirror. The joiner loads the host's colony from a save built in memory, its simulation is frozen, and its actions are replayed on the host. Players have no avatar; other players' building and component previews show with their name. Steam invites or direct IP (TCP 47610). Windows, or Linux through Proton. Two-copy automated suite under Proton 16/16 with mutation twins (direct IP); the author reports two-PC sessions joined through Steam invites. Tested with two players only. One-file installers for Windows (.bat) and Linux (.sh) install BepInEx and the mod with SHA-256 checks. MIT. Write-up in games/planetbase.

games.title: Balatro
games.notes: Two windows on one PC (TCP on 127.0.0.1), each player with their own run (money, jokers, deck, shop); the blind score is shared and the host picks blinds, skips and the boss. Options for shared hand levels, both skip tags to both, shared secret hands. Co-op state lives in the game save, so Continue works after a crash of either window. Lovely 0.9.0, no Steamodded; text in all 15 game languages. Bot suite of 9 scenarios with real game clients (restarts, tag stacks, out-of-hands), plus playtests to ante 8. MIT.

games.title: Balatro
games.notes: Version 0.2.2 alpha (2026-10-13). Both players play the same run: combined blind score, synchronized progression, shared shop, separate decks. TCP port 22122; LAN or a TCP tunnel (IP:port); same PC with 127.0.0.1. Needs Steamodded and Lovely. No source repo or license listed on the package page.

games.title: Fallout Tactics: Brotherhood of Steel
games.notes: Campaign co-op for 2 to 4 players sharing one squad, built from zero on the game's own lockstep multiplayer layer (a DLL loaded by FTSE), MIT. Every player can order every squad member; the host's campaign is played and its save is copied to joiners, who can drop in mid-mission. Synced on top of the lockstep: conversations, quest variables, shops (pausing nobody), recruiting, level-ups, looting, turn-based combat (Individual and Squad), the host's settings, the world map (the host travels, everyone sees it, map pings in each player's colour) and random encounters; a drift check corrects positions, HP, inventories, equipment and the entity table without a reload. Bot tests drive 2 to 4 real game copies on one PC; played by people on two PCs on one home network. Needs GOG 1.27 and FTSE 0.60a. Beta v0.10.4-beta (2026-10-30). See games/fallout-tactics.

games.title: Slime Rancher 2
games.notes: MelonLoader 0.7.3 + Starlight mod; 0.3.9 needs game 1.3.0 exactly and Starlight 4.0.4 (README says 4.0.3). README table syncs slimes, plots, gadgets, drones, money, weather, NPC talk; player inventory not synced; Gray Labyrinth and Sanctuary partial. UDP 1919 with UPnP auto-host, no Steam relay. Automated 2-client test (money, player presence), run by Co-op Anything and not by the mod's author, passed on Steam 1.3.0; see games/slime-rancher-2. GPL-3.0.

games.title: Slime Rancher 2

games.title: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic
games.notes: GPL-3.0 fork of reone (the seedhartha engine reimplementation) adding online co-op to the KotOR 1 campaign. alpha-0.4.0, 2026-10-15. Story Mode has a host run the story and guests take the party's companions; Free Mode lets guests bring their own characters. Host runs the authoritative simulation and guests send intent; the campaign, enemies and world state are shared, though store, workbench, minigame and Free Mode/chargen flows are not yet gated, so the story scope is partial. Optional join-code service for short codes (direct ip:port works without one). KotOR II's install is optional - it supplies the KotOR II interface and systems, but the game plays KotOR 1 with the KotOR HUD without it. Verified 2 clients on one PC over localhost (direct-ip) with a 77-gate scripted suite run on alpha-0.4.0, published alongside this write-up; not rerun on the current alpha-0.4.4. Two packaging fixes (wrong VC++ runtime; KotOR II treated as required) are an open pull request to the fork (McChaffeeFAF/kotor-coop#1), not yet merged. Source-only, no releases, builds from source.

games.title: A Difficult Game About Climbing
games.notes: Ghost co-op: every player climbs their own physics climber and sees the others as tinted, name-tagged copies; optional rope pulls players together. BepInEx 5 plugin with Steam lobby plus SteamNetworkingMessages using the game's own Steamworks.NET (no extra DLLs). Tested only as two game windows linked over localhost UDP and by creating one Steam lobby; no two-account Steam session yet. World objects are not synced and players do not collide. MIT, plugin source in its own repo. Tested on Steam build 20993968. Write-up in games/a-difficult-game-about-climbing.

games.title: XCOM 2: War of the Chosen
games.notes: Two players split the squad on campaign missions (tactical layer only, no shared strategy); soldiers can be imported from the friend's game; no Ironman. Workshop status "Final", last update 3 Sep 2017, five days after War of the Chosen came out, so probably for the base game only. No public source found. Write-up in games/xcom-2.

games.title: XCOM 2: War of the Chosen
games.notes: Prototype of a shared campaign, strategy layer only, for developers (no player build yet). Both players run the same Avenger; one player at a time holds a baton and edits (research, building, armory, Geoscape...), every frame goes to the partner as a merge game state with a fingerprint; edit screens ask for the baton, HUD panel with "ask for control". Join by full history transfer. Tested with two game instances on one PC over direct IP (Steam buildid 8270065, WotC + DLC) and a scripted suite asserting equal state on both; scope is one PC, no two-PC or Steam session yet; no tactical co-op. Write-up in games/xcom-2.

games.title: Cult of the Lamb
games.project: Cult of the Lamb Co-op Anything
games.notes: Online co-op over a Steam lobby, built on COTLMP by GeoB99 (MIT). The friend joins from the main menu and plays on the host save as the Goat. Dungeon runs share the layout, enemies, enemy health, kills and pickups. Installer included. Pre-release v0.9.4 (2026-10-30). The README reports scripted tests with two game copies on one PC and a loopback Steam stand-in, and says real two-account Steam play is not tested yet; we did not re-run the tests.

games.title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas
games.notes: Story co-op for two over the network. The host runs the save and starts missions, and a mission begins once both players stand in the marker. Cutscenes play for both, pedestrians, traffic, police and gangs are shared, vehicles work for both, and each player keeps their own money, skills and look. Needs GTA San Andreas 1.0 US (the README points Steam and Rockstar Launcher owners to a downgrader). The host shares a connection code; it opens the port through UPnP or NAT punching, with an optional relay. v0.3.2 (2026-10-29). MIT. English and Russian README.

games.title: FEZ
games.notes: Online multiplayer where players see each other in the world with customizable names; the README lists text chat, co-op gameplay, competitive modes and spectator mode only as future ideas. Needs the HAT mod loader (v3.0 or later for v0.8.0). Players connect to a server you run yourself (port 7777 by default) or to someone else's, set in the mod's ini file. v0.8.0 (2026-10-07). MIT.

games.title: Gothic 1 Remake
games.notes: Early prototype. A native DLL is injected into two running game instances and each player sees the other as a puppet with the full skeleton pose (walking, running, crouching, jumping, sword draw and attacks, eating) and equipment, over UDP. Verified on one PC with two windows, including through Couchlink; joining by IP between two PCs is implemented but not tested between different PCs. No shared NPCs, combat, quests or saves. Works only with one exact game build. No prebuilt binaries, you build it. MIT. Not affiliated with Alkimia Interactive or THQ Nordic.

games.title: Noita
games.notes: Online true co-op for Noita. The README lists as synced: players with positions, health, perks and inventories, wand and item usage, items in the world, enemies and their attacks, the pixel grid world, fungal shifts and polymorphing. A proxy app downloads and installs the mod; the README also covers Linux and macOS. v1.6.8 (2026-10-20). Apache-2.0. A showcase video and an active Discord are linked from the README.

games.title: Rick and Morty: Virtual Rick-ality
games.notes: BepInEx 5 plugin for the Steam VR build; two players, each a Morty-clone head and hands. The host's game is in charge. Shared are grabbable items (host-granted ownership with epochs, hand-offs, throws), doors, levers, sliders, buttons and pull cords, the story graph's events and stage, scene and mission-area changes, Rick's and Morty's lines and animations (dice seeded the same), things the game makes or destroys, enemies (aim at the nearest player), and the final boss. Each player dies and respawns on their own; only the host saves. Late joiners skip a scene's opening lines. A flat-screen mode (`-vrmode None`, keyboard and mouse) can play with a headset player. Putting a part into an attach point (the computer's RAM stick, crystal, fuse) stays on the player's own side in v0.7.0. Steam lobbies and P2P through the game's own Steamworks, or LAN/direct TCP 27040. v0.7.0 pre-release. The lab runs two or three minimized game copies without a headset through scripted tours (LAN, 120 ms lag, Steam lobby, all mission areas) with error and desync checks, plus a mutation check per fix. Two Steam accounts and real headsets are not covered by the lab. Source is public with no licence file yet.

games.title: Overgrowth
games.notes: Engine fork with rewritten movement replication (local player simulation, snapshots, clock sync), a story co-op mode, revive, server browser, Steam friend join and direct IP. Nine days old, one author, daily builds; release 0.40.0 (2026-10-23). Apache-2.0. Bundled "Overhaul" mod is optional but must match across players. Tested with two real clients on one PC (games/overgrowth): join, first story level with its cutscene, movement sync and a level change pass; a join is refused when Workshop mods are subscribed (order-dependent mod check, bug reported in the write-up). Enemies, items, dialogue choices, checkpoints and deaths not yet checked.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword
games.engine: Nintendo in-house (EGG / NW4R g3d), Wii; decompilation zeldaret/ss
games.notes: Wii USA disc SOUE01 revision 0 in Dolphin 2609a, each player with their own dump. A bridge next to each Dolphin reads and writes guest memory and talks UDP (host forwards one port); a REL built from the zeldaret/ss decomp replaces the unused J_TEST actor and draws the other player as a second Link (models, outfit, real animations, sword, shield, held items). Story, item, scene, dungeon (keys), chest and enemy defeat flags are shared and written to both save files; loads and resets cannot erase the other player's progress. Live enemies are owned by the nearer player (epochs, following playbook/actor-ownership.md); the other game shows them at the owner's position with shared (lower) health, and Keese, ChuChus, Remlits and Skytails also with the owner's animation. Enemies only damage their own game's Link. A two-PC internet session was played with version 0.1; later features are covered by an automated two-client bot test (21 checks, Skyloft, see games/skyward-sword).

games.title: Cuphead
games.notes: Online version of the game's own two-player co-op, by Germanized (with Sh0kr). BepInEx 5 plugin with Steam lobby invites and Steam P2P (ISteamNetworking with relay allowed, so no port forwarding). Host owns the world, scenes, save and bosses; the guest plays Player Two on a mirror of the host's save. Last release v1.6.2 (2026-10-15). Source is public but the repo has no license file. Continued in the Multiplayer Everything fork (separate entry).

games.title: Cuphead
games.notes: Fork of Germanized's CupHeads, v1.7.0 pre-release (wire protocol 4). Adds a LAN/direct-IP TCP fallback (port 27140), a mod-only BepInEx ZIP instead of the installer, and a fix that reconciles the partner's cup health and death or revive with its owner. A same-PC lab with two game copies over the LAN fallback passes 15 checks (connect, world map, both cups moving, level load, boss HP, guest hits and death, revive by heart and by parry, back to the map); 6 mutants that each drop one sync path are all caught, and a 7th shows the health backup covers lost hit packets. Steam P2P between two real accounts is not yet tested. Write-up in games/cuphead.

games.title: Zoo Tycoon
games.engine: Blue Fang proprietary (C++, DirectDraw); built on openzt
games.notes: Host-authoritative co-op as a patch on openzt (GPL-3.0). A friend joins by IP and receives the host's zoo; budget, date, pause, admission price and research are shared, and everything either player builds, sells, fences in (exhibits with their gate), lays as path, terraforms, adopts, hires, moves or fires appears on both copies; the host's animals and staff (positions, births, deaths) are mirrored once a second; each player sees the other's map cursor. Guests and animal needs are per copy. Tested with a two-copy lab (35 checks, 11 mutants) on the Complete Collection, zoo.exe 12.4.0.9; freeform only, scenarios untested; no two-PC test yet. Write-up in games/zoo-tycoon.

games.title: Dynasty Warriors 3: Complete Edition Remastered
games.project: Official split-screen co-op (shipped) and online co-op (free update announced)
games.notes: Ships with 2-player local split-screen co-op and versus only; Steam does not list Remote Play Together. Koei Tecmo announced at TGS 2026 a free update adding online 2-player co-op, due by January 2027 (not released as of 2026-11-01). No community online mod found. Research only, see games/dynasty-warriors-3-remastered.

games.title: TimeShift
games.engine: Saber3D (Saber Interactive), Direct3D 9, Havok, FMOD, Bink; own event-driven level script language
games.notes: Whole story campaign over the game's own netcode (host plays the story, clients replay it), 2 to 4 players on a LAN or by direct IP (the Internet list is revived through OpenSpy, not yet tested between two homes), and two players on one PC in split screen. Version 0.1.1; a dinput8.dll proxy plus data built at install time from the player's own archives (no game files in the repo); needs patch 1.2, Steam copies (patch 1.0) are brought to 1.2 only with the player's explicit consent and their own community update package. Slow and stop time powers for everyone, reverse, AI on clients (deaths, corpses, shots and their sound), levers, mounted guns and quad on clients, Regroup, gate hints, Continue with the real loadout of the host and each client. One-file setup exe, installer in six languages and a shortcut that installs newer releases from GitHub before each start. A bot runs a host and a client through all 24 levels with the level changes; a whole campaign played by people, Internet play and sound judged by ear are still to come. Soldiers' voices and gibbing sounds are host-only. MIT. Write-up in games/timeshift.

games.title: Alien: Isolation
games.project: AI co-op (build from zero, this fork)
games.notes: Build-from-zero presence co-op. A mock steam_api.dll plus a narrow two-jump patch of AI.exe lets a second instance boot; an in-process D3D11 probe (coopnet.dll) syncs player position and facing over UDP at 20 Hz and draws the peer as a body-shaped, screen-space avatar in both instances, with snapshot interpolation, a 1.5 s peer timeout, and an edge arrow when the peer is off screen or behind the camera. Each player is in their own world (no shared enemies/doors/items); both must load the same mission save. Occlusion was attempted via depth sampling at Present and found not viable (the depth buffer is cleared before Present); the avatar draws through walls. Packaging scripts (install/host/join/local2p/status) provided. Tested with a two-instance harness (wingame/tile/keys/ocr/winshot/pix) on a 3440x1440 rig, side by side on one display.

games.title: State of Decay
games.project: State of Decay CryEngine coop mod
games.notes: Prototype for the 2013 Steam release (app 241540, build 305948). Undead Labs cancelled official co-op in 2013; no earlier published shared-world mod was found. Uses the build's dormant CryEngine netcode on isolated test copies (never the Steam install). Up to four players on LAN can join, see each other, walk, and fight zombies together; missions, community and journal stay host-only, and joiners beyond the second player have limited survivor records. Results depend on runtime helpers under gitignored local/ (host_boot_coop, join patches, coop_setup, etc.) and cannot be reproduced from the write-up alone. No installable co-op build. Write-up in games/state-of-decay.

games.title: Spore: Galactic Adventures
games.notes: Cell stage only, the first of SPORE's five stages; after Cell the mod shows an end screen instead of the landfall transition, so Creature, Tribal, Civilization and Space have no co-op at all. A native C++ client (Spore ModAPI plus Detours, pinned to the executable by hashed RVA) talks to a separate C# TCP session server that brokers state and broadcasts player positions, appearance, NPC snapshots and world actions. Supported setup is two windows on one PC with two ModAPI Launcher Kit installs and a second profile at %AppData%\SporeCoop2; remote play between computers is unfinished and world transfer between machines is not implemented. Latest release v1.0.1 (2026-09-27, protocol 10), 21 commits in 10 days and no issues tracker. The licence is ambiguous - the LICENSE file is MIT, but the core sources (native/Probe.cpp, server/SessionServer.cs and 18 other files) carry SPDX-License-Identifier GPL-3.0-or-later headers and the rest carry none, so the project as published is MIT plus GPL-3.0-or-later code. Release zip SHA-256 verified against the published sum. Verified on the Steam October 2024 build (app 24720, exe 25 066 744 bytes, version 3.1.0.29) on 2026-10-21, where the mod's own scripted suites pass (142 protocol assertions plus native source invariants) and two real game clients were launched end to end and both completed a handshake with the session server, which logged Connected host and Connected guest. Two launch steps the upstream README omits were needed, a steam_appid.txt file with the app id 24720 in the game folder, without which the game exits with code 53, and a second copy of the ModAPI Launcher Kit per window, because the kit overwrites its own mLibs\SporeModAPI.dll on every launch. Still not verified are two players in one world, because the invite flow is in-game UI clicks with no scriptable trigger, and the 154 native engine checks, which need a test binary that is not shipped in the release and cannot be built without MSVC. Upstream itself still stops at the Cell stage; a fork with a Creature-stage transition patch is listed separately below.

games.title: Spore: Galactic Adventures
games.project: Spore Multiplayer Mod, Co-Me fork (Creature-stage patch)
games.notes: Fork of emerald194520350-alt/spore-multiplayer-mod with one commit on top of upstream v1.0.1 that lets a live cooperative session continue past the Cell stage. Upstream intercepts the landfall and shows an end screen; the patch reports the Cell stage completion to the session server, lets the native landfall and the land editor run, and reports the entered stage with a new stageTransition message that the server validates, advances and broadcasts to both windows. The protocol stays at 10 and the message is additive, so an unmodified upstream client still connects. The Cell stage completion became a fact about the shared world and survives a server restart, and the shared stage is persisted. Creature-stage gameplay synchronisation is NOT implemented - two players still do not see each other's creature, a shared planet, shared herds or creature interactions, and the Creature simulator stays local to each window. Verified on the Steam October 2024 build (app 24720, exe 25 066 744 bytes, version 3.1.0.29) on 2026-10-22 - the fork builds from a clean checkout with MSVC v143, its own suites pass (148 protocol assertions, 119 native assertions, the source invariants), a new end-to-end test drives two real native clients through the real invitation handshake against the real session server and moves the shared world from cell to creature over TCP, and the rebuilt DLL was loaded into two live game windows that both completed the handshake. NOT verified - the Cell stage was never played through to its end in a running game, so the landfall, the land editor and the stage report still need one interactive confirmation, and Creature-stage gameplay was not tested at all. The patch is released under GPL-3.0-or-later; upstream's LICENSE file says MIT while its core sources carry GPL-3.0-or-later SPDX headers, and that upstream inconsistency is left untouched.

games.title: Spore: Galactic Adventures
games.notes: The only Spore co-op project that aimed past the Cell stage, and the only one with online rooms. GPL sources are published with the installer (installer, launcher and native mod). The live service is paused, the release endpoint answers 503 Release unavailable and the lobby answers 426 Update SporeCoop in the launcher before playing. The shipped build id is cell-preview.27, and the site lists Civilization and Space as coming later, so even a working service would not have delivered the Space stage. The launcher identifies the game build by exe size and version and accepts the October 2024 Steam build (25 066 744 bytes, 3.1.0.29), which matches this owner's install, and the release policy is RSA signed with the exe hash in a games set. Playable stages per the site are Cell, Creature and Tribe with up to four players.

games.title: Spore: Galactic Adventures

Its byte level build guard is pinned to the GOG executable (24 895 536 bytes), so it rejects the Steam build this owner has and would need re-qualification first. The changelog reaches 0.1.14 (2026-09-27) and describes meeting across two prepared Creature locations, travelling, saving and reconnecting, and says in so many words that multiplayer gameplay is still in development. The main branch checkout is dated 2026-10-10.

games.title: Mad Max
games.notes: Functional 2-player parallel co-op mod for Mad Max (Max & Chumbucket). Max drives the Magnum Opus while Chumbucket operates rear mounted harpoons/weapons, mid-drive hood repairs, or dismounts on foot with Blackfinger Zeal and pipe wrench brawling. Complete removal of slow-motion time dilation, Bink2 intro skip, and save isolation. Verified with automated multi-instance test suite on Steam build 1398848. Claim issue cranebeaker/coop-anything#180.

games.title: IRON NEST: Heavy Turret Simulator
games.notes: BepInEx 6 (be.785) IL2CPP plugin, clean-room, MIT. Host-authoritative; guests' mission logic is switched off and their presses run on the host. 1.0.2 (2026-10-30). The bot suite passed 37 of 38 scenarios on 1.0.1, and the 1.0.2 regression passed on BepInEx be.785 and be.788. A five-mission soak test ran with two guests (three players). A full campaign mission was played to the end by two real players over Steam on 2026-10-29. Not hardened against a malicious player who already joined. Write-up in games/iron-nest-heavy-turret-simulator.

games.title: IRON NEST: Heavy Turret Simulator
games.notes: BepInEx 6 (be.785) IL2CPP plugin by Jager2251, also shipped as a standalone package with BepInEx. Steam lobby with a hex lobby code, kick and ban, same-version check. Shares mission start and end, turret aim, gun loading and firing (host-authoritative firing values), doors and hatches, shell paint, fire-mission cards (ticks shared, deleting not), map drawings (host toggle), the supply console (ammo, charges, points, repositioning, recon plane), and soldier avatars with name tags. Not shared on purpose are music and artillery-computer inputs. Joining a running mission is unsupported (the late joiner desyncs). High Command and Field Report texts show in the host's language. Versions 2.0.0 and up are for the game's full release; built against BepInEx be.788, with a Proton note for Linux. 2.5.0 (for the game update that added unit behaviours, map area effects and per-shell hit tracking) syncs damaged and destroyed units, unit behaviours and movement, map area effects, one random seed per mission (enemy fire, spawns, targets, shell spread), mission statistics on the end screen, and the mission clock, with counter-battery fixes (from its Nexus changelog). The GitHub repo is the issue tracker and holds no source; players file bug reports there. CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Nexus first upload 2026-08-04; 2.5.0 on 2026-10-28, with about 16k unique downloads and 83 endorsements on 2026-10-30.

games.title: IRON NEST: Heavy Turret Simulator
games.notes: Host-authoritative BepInEx IL2CPP plugin over a Steam star topology, built with AI coding agents (stated in its README). The README lists as synchronized mission flow, crew avatars (station attachment, head look, locomotion), the tactical map, ballistic calculator, requisition, gun loading, turret and fire control, operations stations (radio, valves, engines, lights, teleprinter, counter-battery, doors), and the cat. It uses ownership leases for controls and snapshots for late join. Ballistic cards stay private until dragged into the world. It targets a host plus four guests; the README says most validation used fewer clients. Status is as stated by the README, and no community reports were found. Source visible, All Rights Reserved. Standalone release v1.1.0 on 2026-08-14.

games.notes: Cross-loader (BepInEx 6 IL2CPP or MelonLoader 0.7.3) host-authoritative co-op over Steam P2P lobbies, with a room password and version check. A LAN TCP transport arrived in v0.2.1-Alpha-2. Its README marks as done turret aim, firing, reload workflow, avatars, the record player, mission objectives, impacts, counter-battery, engine, pressure and lights ("main paths done; remaining edge cases tracked"), punchcards by card id, and mid-join snapshots. It also has a custom mission framework and a dual-instance loopback test mode. AGPL-3.0. Latest v0.2.1-Alpha-2 on 2026-09-12.

games.notes: A VR mod with multiplayer by Blah64 (BepInEx 6 IL2CPP, developed against be.764, OpenXR, Silk.NET). Up to three other players can join one nest for co-op, or split across two nests for PvP, with flatscreen crossplay. F7 opens a lobby browser. games.title: Middle-earth: Shadow of War
games.notes: One host and one client, UDP, direct address over an overlay VPN. The host's world is the real one; the client joins the host's save (SHA-256 checked), sees the host's enemies (up to 16 near either player), hurts them and is hurt by them, and follows the host's fast travel. MIT, Steam build 3095001 only; runs in a separate copy of the game folder with saves and Steam cloud redirected and the game itself offline. Tested only with two game copies on one PC (loopback and a simulated bad network, scripted checks plus an offline suite); never on two PCs. Slow motion is not off in co-op yet, captains and Nemesis events are the host's only, the client cannot fast-travel by itself. Research and reverse-engineering notes are in games/shadow-of-war; claim issue cranebeaker/coop-anything#93.

games.title: Superflight
games.notes: Plugin for the author's own SFMF mod loader (Unity UNet, direct IP, port 4444, host also plays). Shows other players as coloured spheres with name and score, and sends the host's world seed so everyone flies the same map; the game has no enemies, items or story. Source committed 2018-12, DLL released 2022-01 with no play reports found; the author wrote in 2025-01 that it probably no longer works and had released the source in 2018 for others to finish. No license stated. Loads only under Phlarfl's launcher 1.2.0, not the maintained SFMF v2 (vicjohnson, MIT, no multiplayer mod). Audit in games/superflight; a new BepInEx plugin (SuperflightMP, own entry) replaces it.

games.title: Superflight
games.notes: BepInEx 5 plugin (MIT, release 0.2.0 from 2026-10-30) for the Steam build. Host-authoritative: everyone flies the host's level (seed sync), remote players are tinted copies of the wingsuit with name and score, and a host-decided choice screen with scoreboard at portals, fall-outs and crashes keeps the group on one level. Direct IP over UDP (host forwards a port or uses a VPN) or Steam friends-only lobby with overlay invites and +connect_lobby on the game's own Steamworks.NET (no port forwarding). Automated two-copy suites (join, seed match, puppets rendered, portal choice) and a one-copy Steam lobby test pass; a Steam game between two accounts has not been played yet. Lobby max 8. No enemies, items or story in the game. Write-up in games/superflight.

games.title: BLACK SOULS II
games.notes: Private build; the code is not public. Each player runs their own copy (Steam 1.0, or the 1.4 patch plus the Spanish fan translation) through a loader that adds the mod to the game's RGSS3 scripts. Shared switches and variables chosen by a census of the event data, joinable battles with shared enemy damage and deaths, players drawn on the map. Direct TCP over a VPN or a forwarded port. The co-op claims come from real-client bot suites (two clients on one PC over localhost); scenario list and PASS counts per build are in games/black-souls-ii/README.md. The sources back the game, year, engine and the two builds tested.
